meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: совершенно верно = quite right, exactly so

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

встать.gloss: to stand up, to get up

meanings.en: to stand up, to get up (out of bed)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stand up, to get up', paired with 'вставать'.

examples.text: Кто первый встал, того и тапки.
examples.trans: First come, first served (whoever got up first gets the slippers).

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ткнуться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to shut up'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Заткнись, Вика, я никогда не делаю ошибок!
examples.trans: Shut up, Vika, I never make mistakes!

examples.text: Заткнись, рыжая, не мешай мне спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Shut up, redhead, do not disturb me working peacefully!

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
A bell or phone. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
colloquial; stressed on the first syllable
A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

meanings.en: nowhere, not anywhere (direction/destination, used with не or нет)
meanings.note: contrast нигде = nowhere (location)

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.en: to be quiet, to keep silent for a bit
meanings.note: politer or softer than молчать in commands

examples.trans: Let's be quiet for a moment.

examples.text: Помолчите, пожалуйста. Не видите, человеку плохо?
examples.trans: Please be quiet. Can't you see someone isn't feeling well?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: usually 3rd person: что произошло? = what happened?

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.en: to sit down, to take a seat
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'садиться'.

examples.trans: He sat down on a chair.
Listen, sit down. Sit down, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Терять время. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.
Терять время. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Играть в футбол = to play football. Common masculine noun meaning 'football, soccer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Самсон, ты же опаздываешь на футбол!
examples.trans: Samson, you are late for football!

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
